body.statement: Lemma (finite equality certificates).  If \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0\), then there are finite real-Nullstellensatz and saturation identities over a finite real algebraic extension of \(\mathbb Q\) certifying that \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\).  If the extension and every polynomial and product in those identities are supplied in expanded exact form, with exponents in unary, deterministic exact verification is polynomial in the total expanded certificate length.
body.justification: A termination theorem is meaningful only when both branches carry finite, size-accounted certificates.
body.gap: Existing effective real-algebraic bounds do not instantiate the complete expanded certificate contract for these rational causal circuits.
body.consumer: Independent proof checkers can validate equality outputs without trusting the computer-algebra system that produced them.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(R_0=\mathbb Q[p_z:z\in\Omega]\), write \(J_{\mathcal I}=\langle f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\rangle\), and put \(L_0=J_{\mathcal I}:s^\infty\).  A zero reduced normal form with respect to a basis of \(K_{\mathcal I}\) is equivalent to \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\), so \(F_{D,y}\) vanishes on the real variety of \(L_0\).  This universal vanishing assertion is a first-order sentence with rational coefficients.  The cited real-closed-field transfer theorem carries it from \(\mathbb R\) to the real algebraic closure \(R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) of \(\mathbb Q\).  The cited real Nullstellensatz over \(R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) then gives an integer \(k\geq1\), finitely many \(q_1,\ldots,q_a\in R_{\mathrm{alg}}[p_z:z\in\Omega]\), and \(h\in L_0R_{\mathrm{alg}}[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) such that
\[
 F_{D,y}^{2k}+\sum_{i=1}^a q_i^2=h.
\]
By the definition of saturation after scalar extension, membership \(h\in L_0R_{\mathrm{alg}}[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) means that there are an integer \(N\geq0\) and \(a_1,\ldots,a_\ell\in R_{\mathrm{alg}}[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) satisfying
\[
 s^N h=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}a_jf_j.
\]
Consequently the finite identity
\[
 s^N\left(F_{D,y}^{2k}+\sum_{i=1}^a q_i^2\right)
   =\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}a_jf_j
\]
is simultaneously a real-Nullstellensatz certificate and a saturation-membership certificate.  Conversely, exact verification of this identity proves the asserted membership by reading the two displayed implications backwards.

Only finitely many real algebraic coefficients occur, so they lie in one finite real algebraic extension \(E/\mathbb Q\).  Encode \(E\) by a primitive element, its square-free minimal polynomial and an isolating interval for the selected real embedding, encode coefficients in the power basis, encode every exponent in unary, and encode every polynomial as its expanded coefficient list.  Schoolbook arithmetic and reduction modulo the minimal polynomial use a number of rational bit operations polynomial in the total expanded input length; collection of like monomials and equality of the two coefficient maps have the same property.  The isolating data certify that the chosen embedding is real.  Thus exact verification is polynomial in the total length of the expanded certificate.  This proves the narrowed lemma.  Nothing in these definitions supplies a uniform numerical bound on the smallest possible \(k,N,q_i,a_j\) or on \([E:\mathbb Q]\), so the proof makes no claim involving \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).
